Now the news in detail, Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah has said that the Narendra
Modi Government is developing a complete ecosystem around cattle rearing from converting
cow dung into biogas and organic fertilizer to processing dairy products and providing
market access to give a new boost to the rural economy. Addressing the state-level
Gopal Aksameelan in Bhopal today, Mr Shah said cattle rears would be among those benefiting
setting the most from the formation of the Ministry of Cooperation.
We have launched White Revolution 2.2.
Under this initiative, we will establish 75,000 new cooperative dairies in villages and strengthen
46,000 existing dairies.
Of the 75,000 new dairies, the largest number will be established in my state of Madhya Pradesh.
On criminal justice reforms, Mr Shah said that once the Bharati-Niai Sahita is fully
implemented, India's criminal justice system will become the most modern in the world.
He said that after full implementation of the BNS, cases should be disposed of within
three years from the registration of an FIR to the Supreme Court.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Koyal has said India is building a network of
free trade relationships that could eventually cover nearly 75 to 80% of the world's economies,
addressing an event organized by the U.S.-Indian Community Foundation in Chicago.
Mr. Goyle said India has significantly expanded its trade negotiations in recent years with
several more talks underway.
He said the growing network would give companies operating from India access to a much larger
international market.
it. Mr. Goyal said that before 2014, India had free trade agreements with economies representing
around $10 trillion in GDP.
Before 2014, our free trade agreements were mostly with smaller countries whose combined
GDP was around $10 trillion. In the last four to four and a half years, we have decided
to enter into FTAs with 38 more developed countries with a combined GDP of around
60 trillion dollars.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's monthly radio program, Manki Baat, completed 12 years today.
The first episode of the program was broadcast on this day in 2014 on the occasion of Vijay
Dashami.
The 138th episode of Manki Baat was broadcast recently.
Over the past 12 years, Manki Baat has provided a unique platform to highlight the positive
transformation taking place across the country and to encourage citizens to participate actively
in India's development journey. Through the monthly program, the Prime Minister shares inspiring
stories of people from across the country who are making a difference in areas including education,
healthcare, environmental conservation, innovation and social service.
Manki Baat is broadcast across Akashwani and Doordarshan networks and is also available
on the AIR news website and the news on AIR mobile app.
The program is also live streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR news,
DD news, the PMO and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
Vice President CP Radhakrishnan emphasized that
economic resilience cannot be separated from social resilience
and that inclusion is the foundation of resilience in a rapidly changing world.
Mr. Radhakrishnan made these remarks during the inaugural address
Congress, at the 5th Cortelia Economic Conclave in New Delhi today, the theme of the conclave
was resilience in an age of flux.
The vice president said democracy and development can advance together, with consensus, inclusion
and responsive policy making, providing the foundation for sustainable growth.
He stressed that true resilience lies in ensuring that no citizen, enterprise or
region is left behind, and called for collective efforts towards building a Vixit Bharat
Once we were the underdeveloped economy, from there we moved on to the developing economy.
From there we are moving towards the developed economy.
We can call ourselves as a developed economy if it is an inclusive development of everyone.
That is where the real development benefit should reach the nook and corner of the country.
Mr. Radhakrishnan emphasized on the need for decisiveness through consensus
in the wake of rapidly changing global priorities, advancing technology, and intensifying climate changes.
In these times of flex, we need decisiveness embodied in consensus that is required more.
We have to debate, we have to discuss, but we have to come to a final conclusion that should be accepted to everyone.
The government has successfully brought back the hard and narco-trafficking kingpin of
Nafbreed Singh from Turkey, sharing this achievement of the country's enforcement agencies, Mr. Shah
said that Nafbreed Singh used to smuggle heroin and methamphetamine to India from Afghanistan
by obtaining Turkish citizenship under the fake identity of Nawab Virk. He added that
the agencies tracked him down, ripping apart veil after veil to unmask his true identity
and secured his deportation. The Home Minister said that Nafbreed Singh has been put
behind bars in connection with multiple cases involving drug trafficking and other crimes.
The 94th Indian Air Force Day will be celebrated on the 8th of this month.
The theme for this year's celebration is Indian Air Force, infallible, impervious and
precise.
More from our correspondent.
To celebrate this year's Air Force Day, various performances will be carried out including
including the Air Force Day Parade, static display of Indian Air Force assets, performances
by Team Shakti, Air Warrior Drill Team, followed by a performance by the Indian Air Force Drummers
Team, and an air display by Heritage Flight.
Static display of fighters, transports, helicopters, surface-to-air and surface-to-surface guided
weapon systems, radars, and one-way attack unmanned aerial systems will also be showcased.
These platforms highlight the Indian Air Force continuing focus on promoting Make in India.
Team Shakti, the Indian Air Force's premier all-women air warrior drill team will also
perform on the occasion.
Sakleya Nahtar, for Akashwani News, Delhi.

Now this vision has been translated into action through Ayushman Bharat Pradhan

In the field of health security, Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojna is
a fully government-funded health assurance scheme.
Under this, eligible families receive a health cover of up to 5 lakh rupees every year.
The scheme offers cashless treatment facilities for secondary and tertiary care in empaneled
public and private hospitals across the country. Pre-hospitalization expenses for up to three
days and post-discharge expenses for up to 15 days are also included. Pre-existing conditions are
covered from day one of the scheme. There is no limit on family size, age or gender under the
scheme. Eligible beneficiaries can avail of the benefits at any empaneled hospital in any state
state across the country, meaning beneficiaries are not restricted to their home state for
treatment.
Furthermore, all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, regardless of their income or socioeconomic
status are eligible for a health cover of up to 5 lakh rupees under Ayushman Bharat PMJ.
The five Indian nationals were rescued after a Kuwait flag tanker was struck by a projectile
in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Indian embassy in Oman said in a post on X Today that it coordinated the rescue
of the five Indians on board, the empty Kazima 3, who were safely brought ashore.
The mission thanked Omani authorities for their continued support and assistance during
the rescue operation.
The Group of Seven, G7 nations have agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil over
four months in an effort to ease soaring fuel prices with the substantial release of diesel
planned in the first 20 days.
The decision came as diesel prices in the United States climbed to record levels, adding
pressure on President Donald Trump and his administration ahead of November's midterm
elections.
Mr. Trump said that European countries had agreed to release large quantities
of diesel from their stocks, and the process would begin immediately.
The G7 and partner countries will make a coordinated release of 100 million barrels over four
months with a substantial amount of diesel to be released during the first 20 days.
The United Nations has welcomed India's approval of the 1.86 lakh crore rupees green energy
corridor phase 3, describing the grid strengthening and battery storage scheme as a major step
that will deliver big dividends for the country's people and economy.
In a statement to a news agency, UN climate change executive secretary Simon Steele said
the initiative would help India harness its growing renewable energy capacity, meet rising
electricity needs and further strengthen its position as a global leader in solar energy.
An earthquake measuring 4.5 on the Richter scale was recorded at around 9.43 a.m.
today in Pongra, Shinde area of Vasma Taluka in Hingoli district. According to preliminary
In the reinformation, the first tremor measuring 3.3 magnitude was recorded at around 7.47 a.m.
A stronger tremor of 4.5 magnitude followed at 9.43 a.m., after which a series of smaller
tremors were reported.
In Nepal at least six people were killed and 10 others injured today.
When a bus overturned in Gandaki province, police said the Kathmandu-bound bus had
18 passengers on board, including the driver.
When it overturned in the Dhawne area of Nawalparasi district, the injured passengers were taken
to provincial hospital for medical treatment.
The Indian Meteorological Department IMD has forecast heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh
for the day.
IMD has also said that conditions are likely to become favourable for further withdrawal
of southwest monsoon from remaining parts of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh,
Moose, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
In Asian games, India won the gold in men's cricket, defeating arch rivals Pakistan in
the 2020 cricket final at Nishin, Japan today. India won the final by 19 runs. Tracing India's
target of 212 runs, Pakistan managed to score only 196 for 6 in their stipulated 20 overs.
Earlier India posted 211 for 6 after opting to bat first. Opener Abhishek Sharma scored
61 of 28 balls, while Tilak Verma remained unbeaten on 51 of 22 balls.
Shivam Dube added 27 of 14 balls to take India past the 200-run mark.
With this, India has secured its 81st Asian Games medal, including 19th goal to the tally.
India has also won 26 silver medals and 36 bronze medals already.
In men's cricket, India were 3 for 1 in 2.3 overs against West Indies in the third
and final odia in Mulanpur, New Chandigarh when reports last came in.
In men's hockey defending champions India will take on Malaysia with the two teams meeting
at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium with eyes on the gold and an LA-2028 Olympics Vota,
the match will start at 3.30pm.
And now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Government developing entire ecosystem based on cattle farming, giving push to rural economy,

And, on the final day of Asian Games, Indian men's cricket team bags gold with 19-run win over Pakistan in finals,
finals in Men's Hockey Finals, India to take on Malaysia in a short while.
And with that, we end the midday news.
